segments.title: Chương 94: Còn báo cáo dự án ấp nở?
segments.content:
Chapter 97 0094 Still Applying for an Incubator Project? (Bonus chapter for Alliance Leader Nevermore)

Guo Feng didn't sleep all night.

On the first official day of school, he was already planning to skip class. His required credits were nearly full anyway.

Chen Guiliang was yawning in the morning. As soon as he got up, he saw Senior Guo's oily, sleep-deprived face.

Then, Guo Feng slapped a few sheets of paper down. "The initial investment will require 130,000 yuan. 80,000 yuan is the minimum budget for hardware. 50,000 yuan is the annual fee for IDC hosting. Additionally, we'll need a development and operations team of at least two people."

If they waited until next year to do this, the annual IDC hosting fee could drop to 20,000 yuan.

"You've already worked out the budget?" Chen Guiliang asked in surprise.

Guo Feng ignored that and continued with his own train of thought, "If I transfer to the Computer Science department, I should be able to apply to use the school's machines. That could save us the 80,000 yuan hardware budget. But that's only temporary, we can't borrow the school's machines forever."

"What about applying for an incubator project?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Guo Feng said, "I don't know anything about that."

"You work on the website's architecture first, I'll go apply for the incubator project," Chen Guiliang said. "Let's discuss the equity distribution."

Guo Feng picked up his mouthwash cup. "Let's talk on the way. I need to get some sleep after breakfast. I already did some work on the website architecture plan last night."

Chen Guiliang also picked up his mouthwash cup. "No need to push yourself so hard."

"When an idea comes, you have to act on it. You can't keep procrastinating," Guo Feng said.

Damn, was this the same lunatic who was pursuing a perfect love yesterday?

"What are you guys talking about?" Min Wenyu was also getting up.

Guo Feng said, "We're planning to build a website."

Min Wenyu didn't inquire further, calling for Jiang Junlai to go wash up with him.

On the way to the public washroom, Guo Feng said, "I don't have many savings, I can only contribute my skills. Do you have money?"

Chen Guiliang said, "I can just about manage 130,000 yuan."

Looks like I have to hurry up and write "Those Things in the Ming Dynasty" to earn some royalties!

Guo Feng was unrealistic when talking about love, but right now he was like a cold machine, performing a rational analysis devoid of emotion. "You're providing the funding and the idea. The idea is irreplaceable, far more important than my technical skills. And I can't contribute any money. You take 90% of the shares, I'll take 10%. How about it?"

Chen Guiliang actually felt a little embarrassed and reminded him, "If we get financing in the future, your 10% will be diluted pretty badly."

"I know. But that's all I'm worth, because my skills are replaceable. You could find many people at Peking University to replace me." Guo Feng was very clear-headed.

Chen Guiliang was a bit thrown off. "Then it's settled."

The bigger the company, the more talent it needs.

A leader also needs a core team as their foundation, otherwise it's easy to have power usurped by a capital-backed appointee.

If a truly vital partner appeared in the future, Chen Guiliang would have to offer up stock options to retain them.

As for this Senior Guo, 10% was indeed about right. If his abilities were exceptionally brilliant, Chen Guiliang wouldn't mind giving him a few more options.

Accepting venture capital was a certainty, otherwise the initial development would be too difficult.

But he had to be wary of capital taking over the nest. His own core team had to be solid!

The 2008 financial crisis would be a good opportunity. Chen Guiliang could use the stock market crash to buy back some shares on the cheap and keep a firm grip on the company.

Jiang Junlai was walking right behind Chen Guiliang, and his face was already a picture of bewilderment.

Today was just the first official day of classes, what the hell was this talk about equity distribution?

Did I miss something?

After washing up, Chen Guiliang ambled over to breakfast, continuing to discuss the website details with Guo Feng.

He didn't understand the technology, but he understood how to state his requirements and have Guo Feng implement them.

Leaving the cafeteria, a weary-looking Guo Feng went back to sleep.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Did he often pull all-nighters like this before?"

Min Wenyu said, "I was a freshman when he was a sophomore, and we've been roommates ever since. That guy, Guo the Madman, is serious in class most of the time, and his daily routine is very regular. But occasionally he'll just snap, maybe he's too stressed and needs to let off steam. I've seen him play video games for several days straight, sleeping through all his classes."

"Is that senior from the biology department very pretty?" Chen Guiliang asked curiously.

"Hahaha!"

Min Wenyu laughed. "He discussed sacred love with you too? That senior isn't exceptionally pretty, but she has this hard-to-describe intellectual quality. Guo the Madman was captivated the first time he saw her. When he got close to her, he couldn't even speak properly. If I hadn't seen it with my own eyes, it would be hard to imagine Senior Guo in that state. It was like he'd lost his ability to think."

The first official class of the semester was "History of Chinese Civilization," an exclusive required course for the Yuanpei Program.

Why was it exclusive?

Because no other department would teach it this way.

It didn't just simply outline the progression of civilization and then give a general overview to the students.

This was an interdisciplinary course, covering multiple fields like history, philosophy, literature, archaeology, art history, and sociology. A single teacher couldn't cover it all; it required the coordinated instruction of multiple professors from these disciplines.

It even included practical fieldwork. For example, the archaeology professor would take students to museums, the Yinxu ruins, Dunhuang... and even to active archaeological sites!

An all-encompassing, deep understanding of the history of Chinese civilization.

The first lecture was on the origins of Chinese civilization, taught by Professor Sun (archaeology), who researched the Xia, Shang, and Zhou dynasties.

This Professor Sun would be seconded abroad next year to work at the Chinese Mission to the United Nations for four years. Opportunities to attend his lectures were running out.

Several archaeological models were placed on the lectern, and a slide was projected onto the screen.

The 140-plus Yuanpei Program students, plus many who came to audit the class, had nearly filled the large lecture hall.

"When we talk about the origin of civilization, it's inseparable from the geographical environment. Let us first analyze the agricultural conditions of the Yellow River and Yangtze River basins..."

Chen Guiliang had arrived neither early nor late, so he could only find a seat in the middle.

He didn't take many class notes, listening with rapt attention instead. If he needed notes to review for exams later, he could just borrow them from a classmate and make copies.

The first class was a double period, lasting 90 minutes.

Professor Sun lectured for 60 minutes, with the remaining 30 minutes for class discussion.

Chen Guiliang found it quite engaging, and during the discussion, he even asked Professor Sun a question.

After class, some students broke into a frantic run. If they were too slow, they wouldn't make it to their next class on time.

Chen Guiliang's next class was "Basic Principles of Marxism," and the professor was also exceptionally brilliant.

At noon, he ran to the library again to copy the contents he needed from the "Veritable Records of the Ming Dynasty."

In the afternoon, more classes.

One of them was a PE class. Tai Chi was a required activity, and he had to choose one other sport.

After school, he went to copy more from the "Veritable Records of the Ming Dynasty."

Back in the dorm at night, he began to write the first chapter of "Those Things in the Ming Dynasty."

On the first day of class, Chen Guiliang's life was incredibly full, so full it felt like he was back in the last semester of his third year of high school...

Who the hell said university was easy and fun?

It was also possible that since it was just the start of freshman year, students didn't dare to skip class yet.

But for Chen Guiliang, he truly couldn't bear to skip. The professors were all so amazing.

A week passed in a flash. On Friday, for "Military Theory," Chen Guiliang finally skipped a class.

To think this thing was mandatory!

Riding his bike to the Peking University Science Park again, the slightly balding man at the incubator project department actually had a vague memory of Chen Guiliang. He remembered upon seeing his student ID; among all those who came to apply for projects, Chen Guiliang was the only freshman.

"Young man, why are you back again? I told you it would be at least 15 business days," the slightly balding man said, amused. He thought Chen Guiliang was being too impatient.

Chen Guiliang took out the business proposal for the campus-wide network. "Sir, I've come up with another project and want to register another company."

The slightly balding man didn't know whether to laugh or cry. "I've never seen anyone like you."

Chen Guiliang said, "I've got a lot of ideas in my head. I can't hold them in, so I just have to try them."

"Let's have it, then."

The slightly balding man was idle anyway. Looking at a project proposal wouldn't take up the few minutes he had for Minesweeper.

Campus-wide network?

The slightly balding man's attitude went from casual indifference to growing seriousness. After finishing, he stood up and extended his hand for a shake. "Hello, student Chen Guiliang. I am Wang Kai, project manager of the Incubation Services Department."

"Hello, Manager Wang," Chen Guiliang greeted him.
